items.question: what does this mean?
items.script:
say This is a matrix equation: a grid of numbers times a vector equals another vector.
highlight 380 170 400 150 | the matrix times x equals b
say Think of it like a recipe: the matrix holds the amounts, and x holds the unknowns we want to find.
ring 655 265 70 | the answer vector b
say Here the lecturer is combining the columns to get the result, which is the answer vector.
title Matrix form of linear equations, Ax = b

items.question: explain this like a story
items.script:
say Picture a snack shop where each column is one snack, and x tells how many of each you buy.
highlight 590 175 80 130 | the snack prices, one column each
say One day, you buy some of each snack and the bill is exactly 0 and 3.
highlight 695 175 80 150 | the total you paid
say The puzzle is to find how many of each snack you bought, which is x.
label 560 330 | combining columns makes the total
say The lecturer is mixing the columns together, just like adding up the cost of your shopping.
title Matrix times x equals b, as a shopping story

items.question: show me step by step how to solve this
items.script:
say First, write the two equations: 2x minus y equals 0, and minus x plus 2y equals 3.
highlight 415 175 90 110 | first column: 2 and -1
say From the first equation, y equals 2x. Put that into the second one.
say Then minus x plus 4x equals 3, so 3x equals 3, and x equals 1.
say Now y equals 2 times 1, so y equals 2.
label 380 300 | answer: x = 1, y = 2
say Check: 2 times 1 minus 2 is 0, and minus 1 plus 4 is 3. Both work.
title Solving a 2 by 2 system, x = 1 and y = 2

items.question: what is a matrix?
items.script:
say A matrix is a neat grid of numbers, arranged in rows and columns.
say Think of a spreadsheet or a seating chart, where every number has its own row and column.
highlight 415 175 250 130 | the whole grid is the matrix
say On this board, each bracketed column is one column of the matrix.
title What is a matrix?

items.question: why do we write it as a matrix?
items.script:
say We write it as a matrix so many equations fit into one short line: Ax = b.
highlight 450 90 270 60 | Ax = b, short form
say Think of it like shorthand: instead of writing every equation, you write one line that holds them all.
say It also helps computers, because the same grid of numbers can be solved with the same steps every time.
title Why write a system as a matrix

items.question: what does the x mean here?
items.script:
say The x stands for the unknown numbers we want to find.
ring 595 120 35 | x: the unknowns
say Think of it like the snack story: x holds how many of each snack you bought.
say In the matrix form, x is a short list of unknowns, one number per column.
title What x means in Ax = b

items.question: what is a system of linear equations?
items.script:
say A system of linear equations is a group of equations that all use the same unknowns.
highlight 30 170 300 50 | equations with n unknowns
say Think of it like a riddle with several clues, where every clue must be true at the same time.
say Each equation is a straight line, so solving the system means finding the point where they all agree.
title System of linear equations

items.question: can you visualize this?
items.script:
say Picture two straight lines on a graph, one for each equation.
say They cross at exactly one point, x = 1 and y = 2, and that crossing is the answer.
say Another view: each column is an arrow, and x tells you how much of each arrow to add.
highlight 560 315 140 45 | combining the columns
say Stretch and add the arrows until they land exactly on b, which is the vector 0, 3.
title Visualizing a linear system

items.question: explain this diagram
items.script:
say This is a neural network that reads a handwritten digit, like the 2 in the box.
highlight 45 88 145 147 | the digit: 28 by 28 pixels
ring 330 330 40 | 784 input pixels
say Each circle is a neuron holding one number, and the lines between them carry those numbers along.
arrow 430 250 -> 520 250 | hidden layers find edges and shapes
say Think of a team of helpers passing notes, each layer finding simpler patterns than the last.
highlight 690 200 50 260 | 10 outputs, one per digit
say The brightest output, here the 2, is the network's guess.
title How a neural network reads digits

items.question: what are these circles?
items.script:
say These circles are neurons, and each one holds a single number between 0 and 1.
ring 470 330 150 | a layer of neurons
say Brighter circles mean a bigger number, like a dimmer switch that is turned up higher.
say Each neuron gets numbers from the layer before it, mixes them, and passes its own number on.
title What a neuron is in a neural network

items.question: what do the lines between them mean?
items.script:
say The lines are connections, and each one has a weight that says how strong that link is.
arrow 530 200 -> 585 320 | one connection with its weight
say Think of water pipes with valves: a wide-open valve lets more flow through.
say A weight can be positive or negative, so it can help a neuron or push it down.
say All these weights together form a matrix, the same kind of grid we saw on the board.
title Connections and weights between neurons

items.question: how does a neural network learn?
items.script:
say A network learns by slowly changing its weights, the strengths of all those connection lines.
say It guesses, checks how wrong it was, then nudges each weight a tiny bit to be less wrong.
say Think of tuning a guitar: pluck a string, hear it is off, turn the peg a little, and try again.
say It repeats this on thousands of example digits until its guesses are mostly right.
highlight 968 68 230 130 | the next video explains the method
title How a neural network learns

items.question: explain this like a story
items.script:
say Once upon a time, a tiny robot looked at a handwritten 2 and had to guess what it was.
highlight 45 88 145 147 | the picture the robot sees
say It sent the picture through its layers, passing notes from one team of neurons to the next.
say At the end, the robot shouted its guess, but at first it was often wrong.
ring 708 265 14 | the guess, and the robot's first try
say Each time it was wrong, it tuned its connection weights a little, until its guesses got better.
title A robot learns to read digits

items.question: what is the input layer?

say Think of it like a row of dimmer switches, one for each dot of the picture.

items.question: what is gradient descent?
items.script:
say Gradient descent is a way to make the network's mistakes smaller, step by step.
highlight 968 68 230 130 | the video on gradient descent
say Think of hiking down a hill in thick fog: you feel the slope under your feet and take a step downhill.
say The hill is the error, and each step tweaks the weights so the error gets a little lower.
title Gradient descent: walking downhill to fewer mistakes

items.question: what is the output here?
items.script:
say The output layer is the last column, with ten circles labeled 0 to 9, one for each digit.
highlight 690 200 50 260 | ten outputs, digits 0 to 9
say Each circle holds a score for how sure the network is that the picture is that digit.
say The brightest circle wins, so here the network's answer is the 2.
title The output layer

items.question: show me visually how information flows

arrow 370 330 -> 455 330 | pixels feed the first layer

arrow 490 330 -> 575 330 | simpler patterns move forward
arrow 605 330 -> 690 330 | final scores for each digit
say The last arrow leads to the ten outputs, and the brightest one is the answer.
title How information flows through the network

items.question: explain how video streaming works
items.script:
say Streaming means the video arrives in small pieces while you watch, not all at once.
highlight 28 530 910 8 | the video loads in small chunks
say Think of a conveyor belt: the server sends the next piece before you finish the last one.
say The gray part ahead of the red bar is the buffer, and the player lowers quality if the internet slows.
title How video streaming works

items.question: what is a variable in python?
items.script:
say A variable in Python is a name that holds a value, like a labeled box.
say For example, age = 15 stores the number 15 under the name age.
say You can change it later, so age = 16 replaces the old value with the new one.
title Variables in Python

items.question: explain recursion
items.script:
say Recursion is when a function calls itself to solve a smaller version of the same problem.
say Think of Russian nesting dolls: each doll opens to reveal a smaller doll, until you reach the tiniest one.
say Every recursive function needs a base case, the tiny doll that stops the calls, or it would run forever.
say For example, factorial(n) returns n times factorial(n minus 1), and stops when n is 1.
title Recursion: a function that calls itself

items.question: what is an API?
items.script:
say An API is a set of rules that lets one program ask another program for something.
say Think of a restaurant menu: you pick a dish from the list, and the kitchen makes it without you entering the kitchen.
say The menu is the API, the waiter carries your order, and the kitchen is the program that does the work.
title What an API is

items.question: what is compound interest?
items.script:
say Compound interest means you earn interest on your original money and on the interest already added.
say Think of a snowball rolling downhill: it picks up more snow as it gets bigger, so it grows faster.
say For example, 100 at 10 percent gives 110 after year one, then 121 after year two, because year two earns on 110.
title Compound interest: interest on interest

items.question: how do I solve 2x + 3 = 11?
items.script:
say Start by getting rid of the plus 3: subtract 3 from both sides.
say That leaves 2x = 8, because 11 minus 3 is 8.
say Now divide both sides by 2 to get x alone.
say So x = 4. Check it: 2 times 4 is 8, plus 3 is 11.
title Solving 2x + 3 = 11

items.question: what is the derivative of x squared?
items.script:
say The derivative of x squared is 2x, and it tells you how fast x squared is changing.
say Use the power rule: bring the power 2 down in front, then lower the power by 1.
say Think of a square with side x: its area is x squared, and when the side grows a little, the area grows by about 2x times that little bit.
title Derivative of x squared is 2x
